blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

A Brief History of Humans and Food

During the journey from our hunter-gatherer ancestors to the present day, there have been three seismic changes that have impacted the food we eat: the discovery of cooking, the emergence of agriculture, and the invention of methods of preserving food.

The 19th-century scientist Charles Darwin thought that cooking, after language, was the greatest discovery made by man. All of us eat some raw food, such as fruit and vegetables, but the great majority of food we consume is cooked. Cooking can turn plants that are inedible into edible food by destroying toxic chemicals that plants often manufacture to protect themselves against attack by insects or other herbivorous animals. These toxic chemicals are referred to as “plant secondary compounds” because they are not directly involved in the plant's normal growth, development, and reproduction, and are produced purely as chemical defenses. They give many of the plants we consume, such as coffee or Brussels sprouts, their bitter taste.

Cooked food is often more digestible because heat breaks down tough cellulose cell walls in plants or tough connective tissue in animals. Chewing raw turnip, a plate of uncooked rice, or a raw leg of lamb is much harder work than eating the cooked equivalent. The energy expended in chewing to break down the tough material is replaced by energy from the fuel used in cooking the food, so the ratio of energy gained to energy expended by the body is greater when food is cooked.

Until the development of agriculture, hunter-gatherers spent up to seven hours a day gathering food. This all began to change around 10,500 years ago with the advent of farming, which led to dramatic changes in human societies. People began to create a variety of new tools to aid survival, and in turn, populations increased in size. These changes led to the possibility of specialization of different tasks within society. Around this time, writing became more sophisticated and allowed people to maintain records of the harvest and taxes. Eventually, formalized structures of government were established as people settled in one area.

The arrival of agriculture meant that, for the first time, our ancestors had more food than they could eat immediately. This, combined with the seasonality of production, led them to discover methods of preserving food: smoking, drying, adding acid by fermentation, or adding salt. These four methods all share one feature in common—they make the food a more hostile environment for bacteria that can cause it to spoil. They also tend to slow down natural chemical reactions in the food that would cause decay.

Although foods today are still preserved in these ancient ways, two more recent methods of preserving food have become more common: canning and freezing. Canning was invented by a Frenchman, Nicolas Appert, in the early 19th century. He sealed food in bottles fabricated from glass and then heated them in boiling water to cook the contents. Appert's method had great advantages over older methods of food preservation: it could be applied to a wide range of foods, and the flavor and texture were similar to freshly cooked products. His idea was soon copied by an Englishman, Peter Durand. Until this point, containers had been too heavy to be widely used, but Durand produced the first ones which were lightweight and resistant to damage. Two years later, in 1812, two Englishmen, Bryan Donkin and John Hall, started the commercial canning of food, although the real rise in popularity of canning had to wait until the invention of the can opener in 1855. Until then, cans were opened with a chisel and hammer. Canning is an extremely effective way of preserving food: one can containing meat, dating back to 1824, was opened in 1939, and the contents were still in good condition.

In the 21st century, the dominance of canning as a method of food preservation has been overtaken by freezing. Chilling food to keep it fresh is an old idea. The earliest mentions of icehouses, thick-walled buildings, half underground, date back to 1700 BC in northwest Iran. In early 16th-century Italy, water was mixed with chemicals to lower its freezing point to -18 degrees Celsius. Several centuries later, frozen fish and other goods were transported by ship from Australia to England. However, the modern frozen food industry was started in the 1920s by an American, Clarence Birdseye. While on a fishing trip with the Inuit in the Canadian Arctic, Birdseye observed that rapid freezing creates smaller ice crystals and therefore causes less damage to food—a discovery he had not expected. Nevertheless, the major growth in demand for frozen food came with the arrival of freezers in ordinary people's homes. The advantages of frozen over canned food include the fact that the flavor and consistency are often identical to the fresh product, and freezing can be used to preserve a wide variety of foods.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

In boxes 1–5 on your answer sheet, write:

  • TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
  • FALSE if the statement contradicts the information

3 Eating cooked food is more energy efficient than eating raw food.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 1
passageNotes.text: 在从我们的狩猎采集祖先到当今的历程中，有三次重大变革影响了我们的食物：烹饪的发现、农业的出现，以及食品保存方法的发明。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 2
passageNotes.text: 19 世纪的科学家查尔斯·达尔文认为，烹饪是人类继语言之后最伟大的发现。我们所有人都会吃一些生食，比如水果和蔬菜，但我们消费的绝大多数食物都是经过烹饪的。烹饪可以将不可食用的植物变成可食用的食物，方法是破坏植物为了抵御昆虫或其他食草动物攻击而经常制造的有毒化学物质。这些有毒化学物质被称为"植物次生化合物"，因为它们并不直接参与植物正常的生长、发育和繁殖，纯粹是作为化学防御手段而产生的。它们赋予了我们食用的许多植物（如咖啡或抱子甘蓝）苦涩的味道。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 3
passageNotes.text: 熟食通常更容易消化，因为热量会分解植物中坚韧的纤维素细胞壁或动物中坚韧的结缔组织。咀嚼生萝卜、一盘未煮熟的米饭或一条生羊腿，比吃烹饪过的同类食物要费力得多。咀嚼分解坚韧物质所消耗的能量，被烹饪食物所用燃料的能量所取代，因此食物煮熟后，身体获得的能量与消耗的能量之比更大。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 4
passageNotes.text: 在农业发展之前，狩猎采集者每天要花多达七个小时来采集食物。大约 10,500 年前，随着农业的出现，这一切开始改变，这给人类社会带来了剧变。人们开始制造各种新工具来帮助生存，人口规模随之增长。这些变化导致社会内部不同任务的专业化成为可能。大约在这个时期，文字变得更加成熟，使人们能够保存收成和税收的记录。最终，随着人们定居在一个地区，正式的政府结构得以建立。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 5
passageNotes.text: 农业的出现意味着，我们的祖先第一次拥有了超出即时食用量的食物。这一点，加上生产的季节性，促使他们发现了保存食物的方法：熏制、干燥、通过发酵添加酸，或添加盐。这四种方法有一个共同特征——它们使食物成为对可能导致食物腐败的细菌更加不利的环境。它们还倾向于减缓食物中会导致腐烂的自然化学反应。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 6
passageNotes.text: 虽然如今的食物仍然以这些古老的方式保存，但两种更近代的食品保存方法已变得更加普遍：罐装和冷冻。罐装是由法国人尼古拉·阿佩尔在 19 世纪初发明的。他将食物密封在玻璃制成的瓶子里，然后在沸水中加热以烹饪内容物。阿佩尔的方法比旧的食品保存方法有很大的优势：它可以应用于各种各样的食物，而且风味和质地与新鲜烹饪的产品相似。他的想法很快被英国人彼得·杜兰德所模仿。在此之前，容器过于沉重，无法广泛使用，但杜兰德生产了第一批轻便且抗损坏的罐头。两年后，即 1812 年，两位英国人布莱恩·唐金和约翰·霍尔开始了食品的商业罐装，尽管罐装真正普及要等到 1855 年开罐器的发明。在此之前，罐头是用凿子和锤子打开的。罐装是一种极其有效的食品保存方式：一罐可以追溯到 1824 年的肉罐头于 1939 年被打开，内容物仍然完好无损。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 7
passageNotes.text: 在 21 世纪，罐装作为食品保存方法的主导地位已被冷冻所取代。冷藏保鲜是一个古老的想法。关于冰窖（厚墙建筑，一半在地下）的最早记载可以追溯到公元前 1700 年的伊朗西北部。在 16 世纪初的意大利，人们将水与化学物质混合以将其冰点降低到零下 18 摄氏度。几个世纪后，冷冻鱼和其他货物从澳大利亚经海路运往英国。然而，现代冷冻食品行业是在 20 世纪 20 年代由美国人克拉伦斯·伯宰开创的。在加拿大北极与因纽特人一起钓鱼时，伯宰观察到快速冷冻会产生更小的冰晶，从而对食物造成的损害更小——这是一个他没有预料到的发现。然而，冷冻食品需求的大幅增长是在普通家庭开始使用冰柜之后。冷冻食品相比罐装食品的优势包括：风味和口感往往与新鲜产品完全相同，而且冷冻可以用于保存各种各样的食物。

items.text:
题目翻译：根据达尔文的观点，烹饪是人类历史上最重要的发展。
答案：FALSE
解析：定位第 2 段 "Charles Darwin thought that cooking, after language, was the greatest discovery made by man." 题干说烹饪是最重要的发现，但原文说 after language（仅次于语言），所以语言更重要，烹饪排第二。

题目翻译：烹饪过程可以去除一些植物毒素。
答案：TRUE
解析：定位第 2 段 "Cooking can turn plants that are inedible into edible food by destroying toxic chemicals." 原文说烹饪可以通过破坏有毒化学物质将不可食用的植物变成可食用的食物，与题干意思一致。

题目翻译：吃熟食比吃生食更节能。
答案：TRUE
解析：定位第 3 段 "the ratio of energy gained to energy expended by the body is greater when food is cooked." 原文说熟食的能量获得与消耗之比更大，即更高效。

题目翻译：Clarence Birdseye 之前在澳大利亚食品行业工作过。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：定位第 7 段。原文先说 "frozen fish and other goods were transported by ship from Australia to England"，后面又说 "the modern frozen food industry was started in the 1920s by an American, Clarence Birdseye"。文章分别提到澳大利亚冷冻运输和 Birdseye 的加拿大北极经历，但没有说明 Birdseye 曾在澳大利亚食品行业工作，因此是 NOT GIVEN。

题目翻译：Birdseye 与因纽特人的旅行证实了他已有的关于快速冷冻的想法。
答案：FALSE
解析：定位第 7 段 "a discovery he had not expected." 题干说 confirmed what he already believed（证实了已有想法），但原文明确说 a discovery he had not expected（一个意外的发现），所以是意外发现，不是确认已有想法。

题目翻译：设备的发展和更大的____
答案：populations
解析：定位第 4 段 "populations increased in size." 农业带来人口增长。

题目翻译：随着文字的发展，保存____的能力
答案：records
解析：定位第 4 段 "writing became more sophisticated and allowed people to maintain records." 文字发展使人们能保存记录。

题目翻译：熏制、干燥以及将食物与酸或____混合
答案：salt
解析：定位第 5 段 "smoking, drying, adding acid by fermentation, or adding salt." 四种保存方法之一是加盐。

题目翻译：Nicolas Appert 把食物放入由____制成的容器中
答案：glass
解析：定位第 6 段 "He sealed food in bottles fabricated from glass." Appert 用玻璃瓶装食物。

题目翻译：保存的食物具有与新鲜食物相同的味道和____
答案：texture
解析：定位第 6 段 "the flavor and texture were similar to freshly cooked products." 原文说 flavor and texture（风味和质地），题目已给 taste（味道），填 texture。

题目翻译：罐头具有____和不易破碎的优点
答案：lightweight
解析：定位第 6 段 "Durand produced the first ones which were lightweight and resistant to damage." 原文说 lightweight and resistant to damage（轻便且抗损坏），题目中 hard to break 对应 resistant to damage，填 lightweight。

题目翻译：金属开罐器取代了与锤子一起使用的____
答案：chisel
解析：定位第 6 段 "Until then, cans were opened with a chisel and hammer." 开罐器发明前用凿子和锤子开罐。

题目翻译：一罐旧的____
答案：meat
解析：定位第 6 段 "one can containing meat, dating back to 1824, was opened in 1939, and the contents were still in good condition." 1824 年的肉罐头在 1939 年打开仍然完好。
